Name the vertices of the net as follows: \(P\) is the top vertex; the top row of the middle strip is \(A,B,C,D\); the bottom row is \(E,F,G,H\); and \(Q\) is the bottom vertex. Then:

- edge \(5\) is \(EF\),
- edge \(x\) is \(HQ\),
- edge \(1\) is \(DH\), etc.

In a regular octahedron, if two triangular faces share an edge, then the two opposite vertices (the vertices not on that shared edge) are antipodal vertices of the octahedron. Denote antipodes by a minus sign. Assign
\[
P=p,\quad A=a,\quad B=b.
\]
Folding successively across the shared edges in the net gives
\[
E=-p,
\]
then
\[
F=-a,
\]
then
\[
C=-E=p,
\]
then
\[
G=-B=-b,
\]
then
\[
D=-F=a,
\]
then
\[
H=-C=-p,
\]
and finally
\[
Q=-D=-a.
\]

Thus the edge \(x=HQ\) has endpoints \((-p,-a)\). But
\[
EF=(-p,-a)
\]
is exactly edge \(5\). Therefore, when folded, edge \(x\) meets edge \(5\).

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
